headline: Attackers raced through freshly disclosed Cisco, VMware, and SharePoint flaws the same day a new Microsoft Defender zero-day proof-of-concept surfaced and a poisoned LiteLLM build exposed thousands of organizations.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers moved fast on freshly patched flaws this week, exploiting Cisco ASA and FTD firewalls, VMware vCenter, and Microsoft SharePoint in the wild as CISA rushed three vulnerabilities onto its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

AI now works both ends of the exploit chain, as Tracebit planted prompt injections beside cloud secrets to disarm attacking agents even while OpenAI shipped GPT-5.6-Cyber with loosened safeguards for exploit development.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Turns Offensive and Defensive Weapon

emerging_trends.text: Poisoned developer tooling keeps rippling outward, with malicious LiteLLM releases traced to the Trivy hack exposing more than 2,500 organizations to credential theft.

topics.title: Actively Exploited Enterprise Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Cisco confirmed attackers exploit CVE-2026-20349 to remotely crash ASA and FTD firewalls, QUIRSO found threat actors abusing VMware vCenter CVE-2026-59310 for code execution and persistent access, CISA verified ransomware gangs now hit a SharePoint remote code execution bug, and CISA added the Cisco firewall, Windows AFD, and Metabase flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: Cisco's CVE-2026-20349, rated 8.6, lets an unauthenticated attacker crash Secure Firewall ASA and FTD devices; VMware vCenter's CVE-2026-59310, rated 9.8, hands intruders arbitrary code and persistent remote access; the SharePoint flaw now anchors ransomware intrusions. Patch all three at once.

sources.title: Cisco warns of ASA and FTD VPN flaw exploited to crash devices
Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access
CISA: Microsoft SharePoint flaw now exploited in ransomware attacks
CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

topics.title: ShieldBreak Defender Zero-Day and Critical Vendor Patches
topics.latest_developments: A day after August Patch Tuesday, the researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse released a ShieldBreak proof-of-concept that bypasses the patch for CVE-2026-50656, the RoguePlanet flaw in Microsoft Defender, to gain SYSTEM; Intel and AMD together fixed more than 80 vulnerabilities; and SAP closed CVE-2026-58231, a perfect-10 unauthenticated code-execution bug in Commerce Cloud.
topics.summary: ShieldBreak revives the RoguePlanet weakness in Microsoft Defender for local SYSTEM control, Intel and AMD patched more than 80 privilege-escalation and code-execution flaws, and SAP's Commerce Cloud fix addresses a maximum-severity unauthenticated code-execution hole. Apply the vendor updates now.

sources.title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldBreak' zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges
ShieldBreak Zero-Day PoC Claims Microsoft Defender Patch Bypass With SYSTEM Access
Chipmaker Patch Tuesday: Intel, AMD Fix Over 80 Vulnerabilities Combined
SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code

topics.title: AI Turns Offensive and Defensive Weapon
topics.latest_developments: Tracebit showed that placing prompt injections alongside passwords and cryptographic keys stored on Amazon Web Services often shuts down attacking AI hacking agents, which obey the injected command; OpenAI launched GPT-5.6-Cyber built to find zero-days and build exploit chains with fewer refusals; and the open-source PentestGPT drives Claude Code or Codex through recon, exploitation, and reporting with no human in the loop.
topics.summary: Defenders now bait autonomous LLM attackers with prompt injections that trip the model's own guardrails, while OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber and PentestGPT automate vulnerability discovery and exploit development. Security teams should test both the traps and the offensive tooling against their environments.

sources.title: Prompt Injections for Defense
OpenAI Launches GPT-5.6-Cyber with Reduced Safeguards for Exploit Development
PentestGPT: Open-source automated penetration testing agentic framework

topics.title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack
topics.latest_developments: CloudSEK reported that two malicious LiteLLM releases sat on PyPI for roughly 40 minutes in March carrying credential-stealing code, and a dataset built from about 434,000 captured files maps potential exposure to more than 2,500 organizations, with the compromise traced to the earlier Trivy hack.
topics.summary: The rogue LiteLLM builds harvested cloud keys, SSH keys, Kubernetes tokens, and database passwords from systems that installed them. Any organization that pulled LiteLLM in March should rotate every secret those systems held.

sources.title: Over 2,500 Organizations Impacted by LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack
Malicious LiteLLM Releases Tied to Trivy Hack May Have Exposed 2,100+ Organizations

topics.title: North Korean Windows Zero-Day Deploys ForestTiger
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported that a North Korean group exploited a fresh Windows zero-day to seize full control of victims' systems and install the ForestTiger backdoor.
topics.summary: The zero-day gave the attackers complete system control and delivered ForestTiger, a backdoor for lasting access. Defenders should watch for a Microsoft patch and hunt for ForestTiger indicators.

sources.title: Fresh Windows Zero-Day Exploited in North Korean Cyberattacks

topics.title: Ransomware Hits Logistics and Local Governments
topics.latest_developments: The Gunra ransomware-as-a-service crew surfaced wielding leaked Conti code and old Fortinet firewall and VPN flaws to bypass MFA against critical infrastructure, a cyberattack halted eight European warehouses of France's CEVA Logistics and rippled to Bol and Steam customers, Wesco confirmed an intrusion that ExfilSquad claims, a ransomware group hijacked a hospital's Facebook page while claiming 6 terabytes of sensitive records, and municipalities in California, Oklahoma, Wisconsin, and Texas shut down services.
topics.summary: A fresh wave of ransomware and extortion crippled supply chains, hospitals, and city halls across two continents. Organizations running Fortinet appliances should confirm patches and hunt for MFA-bypass activity.

sources.title: Gunra Ransomware Gang Exploits Fortinet Flaws, Bypasses MFA
Cyberattack on logistics giant Ceva hits retailers and Steam customers across Europe
Local governments in four states dealing with cyberattacks that have shut down services

business_politics.title: Hormuz Standoff Deepens Oil Demand Slump
business_politics.latest_developments: The International Energy Agency said the Strait of Hormuz standoff will drive a deeper contraction in global oil demand this year, and crude extended its gains as traders discounted any imminent deal to reopen the waterway.
business_politics.summary: Renewed Middle East hostilities and the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz keep pushing fuel prices up and weighing on consumption, holding oil elevated while markets doubt Iran and its neighbors will restore passage soon.

business_politics.title: Vance Presses Ukraine to Halt Tanker Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported that Vice President JD Vance asked Ukraine to stop drone strikes on tankers collecting Kazakh oil at Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, which Washington fears will choke global crude supply.
business_politics.summary: Kyiv's drone attacks on vessels loading Kazakh oil at Novorossiysk alarmed Washington, which worries the campaign threatens supplies moving through an export route entangling both Russian and Kazakh crude.

sources.title: JD Vance asked Ukraine to halt strikes on tankers using Russian port

business.title: RK Mellon Backs Rare Disease Hub
business.latest_developments: The Richard King Mellon Foundation pledged $25 million on August 12 to launch a rare disease therapy hub in Pittsburgh.
business.summary: The Pittsburgh-based foundation's grant seeds a center meant to speed treatments for rare diseases, deepening the region's life-sciences ambitions.

sources.title: RK Mellon Foundation pledges $25M to launch rare disease therapy hub in Pittsburgh

business.title: Springdale Weighs Data Center
business.latest_developments: Springdale-area residents aired concerns over a proposed data center, and State Senator Lindsey Williams said such projects are inevitable but should be built to benefit host communities.
business.summary: A data center planned for the Alle-Kiski Valley town of Springdale drew resident worry; Williams, whose district covers the area, wants developers required to deliver community benefits.

sources.title: Springdale-area residents express their concerns about a data center coming to their town

around_town.title: Red Light Cameras Go Live
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh switched on automated red light enforcement August 12 at North Dallas Avenue and Penn Avenue in Point Breeze and a second intersection, opening a 60-day warning period before citations begin.
around_town.summary: The city's new camera system targets intersection safety; drivers who run the lights at the two locations receive warnings for 60 days before the fines start.

sources.title: Automated red light enforcement begins today in Pittsburgh. Here's what to know.

around_town.title: ICE Eyes Buying Moshannon Center
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported that ICE may try to buy the Moshannon Valley Processing Center in Clearfield County when its contract expires next month, to keep detention capacity in Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: The agency now runs the immigrant detention facility through a contract with Clearfield County and a private owner; a purchase is among the options it weighs to hold beds in the state.

sources.title: ICE considering buying immigrant detention facilities, other options to maintain capacity in Pa.

around_town.title: McKeesport-Duquesne Merger Draws Pushback
around_town.latest_developments: Community members pushed back at a meeting against a possible merger of the McKeesport Area and Duquesne City school districts.
around_town.summary: The two Mon Valley districts are weighing consolidation, and residents turned out to voice opposition, KDKA reported.

sources.title: Community members push back against possible merger of McKeesport and Duquesne school districts

events.title: Science of Speed Opens
events.latest_developments: Science of Speed, a state-of-the-art indoor go-kart track just outside the Kamin Science Center on Pittsburgh's North Shore, opened to the public last week.
events.summary: The new indoor karting attraction lets visitors test their driving at the Kamin Science Center, the North Shore museum formerly known as the Carnegie Science Center.

sources.title: Science of Speed opens at Kamin Science Center

events.title: Little Italy Days Returns to Bloomfield
events.latest_developments: The 26th annual Little Italy Days opens Thursday, August 13, in Pittsburgh's Bloomfield neighborhood and runs through the weekend.
events.summary: The Italian street festival brings food, music, and vendors to Bloomfield, the city's traditional Little Italy.

sources.title: Daisy checks out Little Italy Days

around_teams.latest_developments: On the August 12 Not Just Football, Cam Heyward and Hayden broke down camp's first live-tackling reps, Saturday Night Lights standouts, and the roster battles brewing at Saint Vincent.

around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported August 12 that Notre Dame product Gabriel Rubio has emerged as a stout run defender with a real shot at the Steelers' 53-man roster.
around_teams.summary: Rubio's run-stuffing at Latrobe has him in the mix as the Steelers sort out their defensive line depth.

around_teams.title: Cruz Rehab Moves to Altoona
around_teams.latest_developments: The Pirates transferred Oneil Cruz's rehab assignment to Double-A Altoona, where he went hitless in his first game with the Curve.
around_teams.summary: Cruz, the Pirates' hard-throwing outfielder, advances his return from injury one level up the farm system as Pittsburgh works him back toward the majors.

team_usa.title: USA Swimming Sidelines CFO
team_usa.latest_developments: USA Swimming placed chief financial officer Cory Hilliard on leave August 11 after learning of his arrest on theft and embezzlement charges tied to a previous job.
team_usa.summary: Hilliard, 54, hired last December, faces charges stemming from his time as an administrator in the University of Colorado athletic department; the sport's national governing body acted once it learned of the arrest.

sources.title: USA Swimming learns of arrest, puts CFO on leave

team_usa.title: Rivera Repeats as Gymnastics Champion
team_usa.latest_developments: Olympic gold medalist Hezly Rivera, 18, rallied from fourth on the final day to win her second straight U.S. women's gymnastics national title August 9.
team_usa.summary: Rivera, a member of the Paris Olympics gold-winning American team, posted four poised routines to capture the national all-around crown.
